key_insight: HTP-Net improves instance segmentation of dense, slender welding material stubs by preserving boundaries, modeling long-range connectivity, and using orientation cues.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stub counting and shape measurement can support welding-factory inventory management.
method: Wavelet-driven edge preservation retains fine boundaries during feature downsampling.
Long-range topology modeling helps maintain connectivity in slender targets.
An orientation-driven segmentation head reduces excessive non-maximum suppression and overlapping-mask artifacts.
evidence_signal: On custom and public dense-material datasets, reported mAP50 gains ranged from 1.2% to 55.3% over existing methods; factory validation reported average recognition accuracies of 99% for electrode stubs and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify inference speed or robustness across lighting and camera setups, which should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
